correctness.rationale: The regular tetrahedral surface is the quotient of the triangular flat torus R²/<(2,0),(1,sqrt3)> by inversion. The geodesic target law equals the nearest of the two periodic source orbits. Four explicitly derived bisector inequalities give a candidate isosceles cyclic trapezoid V_s of area sqrt3; the actual nearest-site Voronoi cell lies inside it and must have area exactly sqrt3 by inversion symmetry and two orbits, proving equality almost everywhere without assuming finitely many images exhaust the lattice. The four exterior disk-cap pieces are interior-disjoint until cyclic vertex radius R_s, yielding the CDF. Polynomial slicing over x∈[-w(v),w(v)], w=1/2+6sv, confirms E D²=1/3 and fourth moment formula. Independent SymPy exact integration reproduced the polynomial identities for symbolic real s. Source eccentricity equals trapezoid circumradius, and derivative of fourth moment is positive on the open segment.
